name: s06-gil
title: The GIL lets one thread run Python at a time
spec: Left: a small box labelled GIL (one token) held by Thread 1 with a solid arrow, Thread 2 waiting with a dashed arrow. Right two panels. Panel CPU-bound code: threads take turns, no speed-up (orange). Panel waiting on I/O: the lock is released while waiting, so threads overlap (green).
cap: The GIL: one thread runs Python bytecode at a time, but threads overlap while they wait on I/O.

name: s06-choosemodel
title: Choosing a concurrency model
spec: A decision tree. Start: what is the work? Branch 1: CPU-bound goes to processes (multiprocessing, ProcessPoolExecutor). Branch 2: waiting on I/O, many connections and async libraries goes to asyncio. Branch 3: waiting on I/O with blocking libraries goes to threads (ThreadPoolExecutor). Green bar: measure before you choose.
cap: Choosing a model: processes for CPU-bound work, asyncio for many async connections, threads for blocking I/O.

name: s06-queue
title: A bounded queue gives backpressure
spec: Left: two boxes Producer 1 and Producer 2 with arrows into a central box Queue(maxsize=N) drawn as a row of cells, some full. Right: two boxes Consumer 1 and Consumer 2 with arrows out. Orange note on the queue: when it is full, put() blocks the producers. Green note: memory use stays bounded.
alt: Producer consumer with a bounded queue
cap: A bounded queue: when it fills, put() blocks the producers, so memory stays bounded.

name: s06-futures
title: Executors and futures
spec: A flow: your code ; executor.submit(fn, arg) ; returns a Future immediately ; worker thread runs fn ; future.result() gets the value or re-raises the exception. A second row note: as_completed(futures) yields futures as they finish (orange).
cap: concurrent.futures: submit returns a Future at once, and result() waits for the value or raises the error.

name: s06-asyncio
title: How the asyncio event loop shares one thread
spec: A central box event loop (one thread) with three task boxes around it: Task A, Task B, Task C. Arrows labelled await hands control back to the loop. A timeline strip under it: A runs, A awaits, B runs, B awaits, C runs, A resumes. Orange note: a blocking call stops every task.
cap: asyncio: tasks share one thread, and each await hands control back to the event loop.

name: s06-breaker
title: A circuit breaker has three states
spec: Three circles in a triangle: Closed (calls pass, green), Open (calls fail fast, orange), Half-open (one trial call). Arrows: Closed to Open labelled too many failures ; Open to Half-open labelled after a cool-down ; Half-open to Closed labelled trial succeeds ; Half-open to Open labelled trial fails.
cap: A circuit breaker stops calling a failing service, then probes it before trusting it again.
